human_tolerance.notes: The Japanese article records it nesting in tree holes, woodpecker holes and nest boxes and feeding in gardens and parks; it is a common year-round bird of Japanese suburbs.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeds April to July, laying 7-10 eggs in one or two clutches in a cavity.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Forms small mixed-species flocks in autumn and winter.

vocalizations.description: The high, penetrating two- or three-note song rendered in Japanese as 'tsu-tsu-pi', sung from a high perch; the Japanese article notes its carrying power.
The nasal 'ji-ji-ji' call that gives the bird its Japanese name, exchanged within flocks.
Sharp 'pitsu-pitsu' alarm note; the species varies its alarm call with the type of predator.

taxonomy.note: The GBIF species match on Parus minor returns usageKey 5844847, rank SPECIES, status ACCEPTED, order Passeriformes, family Paridae, genus Parus, authorship Temminck & Schlegel, 1848. The English article on the cinereous tit treats Parus minor as the group of eastern subspecies that were formerly a separate species.

external.note: gbif_usage_key 5844847 from the GBIF species match; inat_taxon_id 339691 from the iNaturalist taxa API, where iNaturalist lumps the Japanese tit into Parus cinereus (Asian tit), so this is the taxon the activity curve is drawn from; wikidata Q973837 from the English Wikipedia page's wikibase item.

range.note: The English article gives P. c. minor as east Siberia (RU), south Sakhalin, central east and northeast China (CN), the Korean Peninsula (KR, KP) and Japan (JP), with island subspecies on Ulleungdo and the Ryukyus. Country codes are a derivation from that prose.

traits.note: The Japanese article gives length about 14.5 cm (13-16.5 cm), wingspan about 22 cm and mass 11-20 g; mass 15.5 g is the midpoint. Locomotion Hop and Fly: tits hop. Diet is from the Japanese article's omnivorous account (fruit, seeds, insects and spiders, preferring small arthropods and seeds), mapped to invertebrate 0.6, seed 0.25, fruit 0.15. Lifespan 3 years is carried from the congener great tit record and is a judgement.

habitat.note: The Japanese article records it nesting in tree holes, woodpecker holes and nest boxes and feeding on the ground and in trees; use arboreal 0.85 / ground 0.15, shelter a cavity, and resources follow the diet and the cavity nest. human_tolerance is Adapter from its abundance in Japanese gardens and parks.

seasonal.note: The Japanese article records breeding April to July with 7-10 eggs in one or two clutches, and small mixed-species flocks in autumn and winter; strategy ActiveYearRound. Juvenile duration 33 days is a judgement from the sourced incubation and fledging of tits.

vocalizations.note: The Japanese article describes the 'ji-ji-ji' call that names the bird, a loud carrying song, and a 'pitsu-pitsu' alarm that varies with the predator. The three calls map onto the program's song, contact and alarm slots.

look.note: The English article describes a grey-backed tit with a black hood, white cheek patch and white wing-bar; the Japanese article adds a black ventral line. Modelled features: the black hood on the head slot, the mirrored white cheek, the black belly line and the white wing bar. Proportions and palette follow the congener great tit record with judgement changes.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: food_tag invertebrate follows the arthropod-heavy diet, song and alarm bind the tsutsupi song and the pitsu alarm, and nest months bracket the April-July breeding season.
